title: The constant module sheaf functor is additive.
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Fix one universe containing the objects and morphisms of $\mathcal C$, the ring $\Lambda$, and all modules considered, as required by this same-universe formulation [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\Lambda_0$ for the constant presheaf of rings, $\Lambda_0(U)=\Lambda$ with identity restriction maps, and $\underline\Lambda=\Lambda_0^\#$ for its ring sheafification [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For a $\Lambda$-module $M$, let $cM$ be the presheaf of $\Lambda_0$-modules with value $M$ and identity restrictions; for a linear map $f:M\to N$, put $(cf)_U=f$. Let $a:\operatorname{PMod}(\Lambda_0)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\underline\Lambda)$ be module sheafification along $\Lambda_0\to\underline\Lambda$ [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], with the sectionwise module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the functor $T=a\circ c$, which is $\mathrm{SheafOfModules.strictPerfectConstantSheaf}\ J\ \Lambda$, is additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]: for any $\Lambda$-modules $M,N$ and linear maps $f,g:M\to N$,
$$T(f+g)=T(f)+T(g).$$

proof.text: For the constant-presheaf functor $c$ in the statement, identity restrictions are semilinear over identity maps of $\Lambda$. A linear map gives a natural transformation because every restriction is the identity; identities and compositions are preserved componentwise. Addition is pointwise: at every object $U$ and $m\in M$, $(c(f+g))_U(m)=(f+g)(m)=f(m)+g(m)=(cf+cg)_U(m)$. Hence $c(f+g)=cf+cg$. This is a componentwise equality of the explicitly defined maps.

proof.text: Let $P,Q$ be presheaves of $\Lambda_0$-modules and $h,k:P\to Q$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], with $\mathcal O=\Lambda_0$ and $\mathcal O^\#=\underline\Lambda$, every map $P\to i(aQ)$ extends uniquely through the unit $\eta_P:P\to i(aP)$; $i$ forgets the sheaf condition and restricts scalars. The definition of $a(h)$ gives $i(a(h))\eta_P=\eta_Qh$, and similarly for $k$ and $h+k$. Since module morphisms and their sums are sectionwise linear [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $i(a(h)+a(k))\eta_P=\eta_Qh+\eta_Qk=\eta_Q(h+k)$. Thus $a(h)+a(k)$ and $a(h+k)$ extend the same map. Uniqueness in the cited universal property gives $a(h+k)=a(h)+a(k)$. No claim that $\Lambda_0$ is already a sheaf is used.

proof.text: Apply step 2 to $h=cf$ and $k=cg$, and use step 1. Then $T(f+g)=a(c(f+g))=a(cf+cg)=a(cf)+a(cg)=T(f)+T(g)$. This is exactly additivity [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. The formula for $T$ is the defining composite of $\mathrm{strictPerfectConstantSheaf}$, so it proves the attached declaration.
